messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: help with installing/running Rattle on Mac:
parts:
Could you send me the output of rattleInfo().

I recently installed rattle on a Mac Air running Lion I think and it worked just fine, so should be possible to do. I'm thinking you might be getting some wrong versions of libraries somehow - which is what the error message is saying.

Do you have Gtk installed through some other application? Might be best if you are able to uninstall Gtk (which is independent of R and Rattle) and then install the RGtk2 package in R which will grab the correct version of Gtk for you.

Regards,
Graham

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: help with installing/running Rattle on Mac:
parts:
Yes - GGobi will be the culprit I think. It does use Gtk. The package list you sent looks good.

So I think what happened is that Ggobi (or as part of you installing GGobi) installed Gtk version 2.18. Please try uninstalling GGobi and uninstalling Gtk 2.18, then try installing RGtk2 again:

> install.packages("RGtk2")
> library(RGtk2)

That should offer to install Gtk and will install the right version. You should then be able to install GGobi again after that.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: help with installing/running Rattle on Mac:
parts:
Hi Graham,
I have the same problem: Try to install rattle on a MacBook Air with Snow Leopard with R 2.13.1. I run rattleInfo() and installed missing packages by install.packages(rattleInfo()). RattleInfo() looks good now (no missing dependencies or old packages), in particular I use RGtk2: version 2.20.17
When I start with rattle(), I get the same error message:

Fehler in rattle() : Versuch eine Nicht-Funktion anzuwenden
Zusätzlich: Warnmeldung:
In method(obj, ...) :
  /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.13/Resources/library/rattle/etc/rattle.ui: required gtk+ version 2.20, current version is 2.18
Rattle timestamp (for the message above): 2011-09-24 11:44:29
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

I have been asked wether rattle() shall install GtK and I confirmed to do so. However, to me it looks like your script installed version 2.18.

I once installed ggobi, but I am pretty sure this was on a different computer. I also deleted the GTK+.framework in /Library/Frameworks and installed it again by running rattle() from R. However, the error stays the same.

Best regards,
Christian

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: help with installing/running Rattle on Mac:
parts:
My apologies - I've just had a look at the source code for the RGtk2 package - it is installing 2.18 of Gtk+ on the Mac (from http://r.research.att.com/libs/GTK_2.18.5-X11.pkg). Note that it is not Rattle that does this - Rattle simply builds on what RGtk2 provides. RGtk2 is installing the Gtk+ libraries and RGtk2 knows better than me what version to install, so this must be okay.

The problme would then seem to be something else, and not this version of Gtk+ as such.

Con you confirm that

> library(RGtk2)

works for you.

If the above works, but rattle() does not, could you try:

> rattle(useGtkBuilder=FALSE)

Given that it is not directly a version issue, we might need to track down which function call is failing in Rattle.

Regards,
Graham

On Sep 25, 2011, at 9:25 PM, Graham Williams wrote:

After an update to current version (per CRAN of rattle and RGtk2).
Before that updated I had a functioning rattle installation. I only
updated after considering the possibility of this failing, since
another user had reported failing to get it working and I just thought
I would "help out". For me it's not really a big deal. In my
experience the install difficulties with 'rattle' over the years have
made me hesitant to put a lot of time into exploring its potential. I
am therefore reluctant to put the rest of my system at risk by doing
major neurosurgery, when the most I have ever done in the operating
theater is to remove a couple of appendices and deliver a few babies.

> require(RGtk2)
Loading required package: RGtk2

> rattle(useGtkBuilder=FALSE)

> rattle(useGtkBuilder=FALSE)
Error in rattle(useGtkBuilder = FALSE) :
The RGtk2 package did not find libglade installed. Please install it.

I have the Urbanek build of GTK+2.18.X11 in the Frameworks section of
my Library directory. The OSX/GTK+ webpage:

http://gtk-osx.sourceforge.net/

.... demands removal of MacPorts and Fink and my reading suggest that
this further implies the need to completely remove any programs
installed through either of those systems. Looking at the potential
impact on my system makes me unwilling to proceed. I see a huge number
of entries when I execute $locate macports in a Terminal session. I am
not sufficiently UNIX-savvy to know if those are just "database
entries" or whether the references to tex and X11 entries represent
essential programs that would be scrubbed with a "complete removal".
And the alternate recommendation to "create a new user" to do the
jhbuild install is not in my programming repertoire.

messages.author: bf23101556263ba5
messages.subject: Re: help with installing/running Rattle on Mac:
parts:
On Mon, Sep 26, 2011 at 8:12 AM, David Winsemius <dwins...@comcast.net> wrote:

....really a big deal. In my experience the install difficulties with 'rattle' over the years have made me hesitant to put a lot of time into exploring its potential. I am therefore reluctant to put the rest of my system at risk by doing major neurosurgery, when the most I have ever done in the operating theater is to remove a couple of appendices and deliver a few babies.


I typically install it inside a virtual machine (say fusion or virtualbox). The 64 bit Linux installations have typically worked well for me, so I just migrate the VM around. I'm due to create a new one (mine was rather dated).

It's not a very mac-like interface anyway, so having it run in a VM doesn't impose any special limitations ... and it removes any concerns about system libraries, fink, etc.

To be honest I typically ran it in VMs on every platform BUT linux (although I probably should have). 

The newest version of fusion can even run LION in a VM, so one doesn't have to learn a new OS to go down the virtual path.

Thanks for the feedback on the Mac install - unfortunately I don't have access to a Mac (this week - currently travelling) to debug, making it a little difficult. My apologies for that.

I need to see where the "attempt to apply non-function" is happening.

Could someone set some debugging on and let me know what function call is failing (send the backtrace):

> options(error=recover)
> rattle()

Can you also tell me the result of:

> Sys.info()["sysname"]

Another thing to try:

> rattle:::fixMacAndGtkBuilderTypes <- function() {}
> rattle()

or else:

> donought <- function() {}
> overwritePackageFunction("fixMacAndGtkBuilderTypes", donought, "rattle")
> rattle()

Thanks for your information and patience.

Graham

messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: [SOLVED] Re: help with installing/running Rattle on Mac:
parts:
Thanks to David Winsemius for assistance in debugging this and Chris
and Illya for further information. The problem will be fixed in Rattle
version 2.6.11 (not yet released).

The issue is that version 2.6.10 of rattle includes a rattle.ui that
claims to require gtk+ 2.20. The third line of rattle.ui contains:

 <requires lib="gtk+" version="2.20"/>

A simple solution while we wait for a new version of rattle is to
manually edit this file to change the 2.20 to 2.16. There appears no
real dependency on 2.20, and 2.18 seems to work just fine.

So, if you can change this line in the installed package then all
should be okay:

 <requires lib="gtk+" version="2.16"/>

(By default this folder may be hidden but should be located in
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.13/Resources/library/rattle/etc/rattle.ui.)

Then the next invocation of rattle() should work.

Regards,
Graham

My thanks to Graham who took the time while he was traveling to talk
me through the debugging process to identify and test the fix.

The other location on a Mac where that file might be found is:

"/Users/<user-name>/Library/R/2.13/library/rattle/etc/"

You can list the possible locations in the R console with:

.libPaths()

The proper file to edit will be in the first lib-path where R can find
a rattle installation , i.e a ...library/rattle/ directory. (My system
had two and the first lib-path was the /Users/... one which was
confusing and I have now fixed that so I know where to find things,)

property" can safely be ignored.
